audience_description: The designated Exams Officer at an Eduversal partner school that holds Cambridge approved Centre status — in many schools this role is carried by the Cambridge Coordinator. The Exams Officer is the school's administrative link with Cambridge International: entries, timetables, access arrangements, secure storage, exam days, script despatch, results, post-results services, certificates and the evidence file. The Exams Officer reports to the Principal, who is Head of Centre and keeps final accountability; the Quality Nominee oversees examination standards and internal moderation. Where a school separates the two roles, the Coordinator owns governance and strategy and the Exams Officer owns logistics and documentation, agreed in writing at the start of the year (Curriculum Module: Exams Officer Handbook 26-27 §1 and §3).

regulatory_anchors.title: Cambridge International Handbook for Centres (current edition)
regulatory_anchors.relevance: Defines Centre obligations: entries, secure materials, Key Times, invigilation, access arrangements, special consideration, malpractice reporting, script despatch and post-results services. Where Eduversal documents and Cambridge differ, Cambridge prevails.

regulatory_anchors.title: Cambridge malpractice and centre staff malpractice rules (Cambridge Handbook)
regulatory_anchors.relevance: The Head of Centre reports all suspected malpractice to Cambridge on the same day, or no later than 12:00 local time on the next working day. Failing to report is itself malpractice.

regulatory_anchors.title: Eduversal Academic Standards — Section 3 (Cambridge Centre Compliance) and Section 10 (Cambridge Examinations Management)
regulatory_anchors.relevance: Network standard for examinations management. The ES 10.3 key dates table is the single home for concrete Cambridge deadline dates in the manual. Where the Exams Officer Handbook and the Academic Standards differ, the Academic Standards prevail.

regulatory_anchors.title: Cambridge Centre Agreement (per school)
regulatory_anchors.relevance: Contractual obligations specific to this Centre.

framework_anchors.live_role_guide: Curriculum Module: Exams Officer Handbook 26-27 (16 sections; Sections 4-11 are used every series).
framework_anchors.induction: Induction Module: Exams Officers 26-27 — a newly appointed Exams Officer runs one full examination cycle with a cross-school guide, ending Certified or Extended.
framework_anchors.annual_dates: Quality Ecosystem: External Exams & Admissions 26-27 and the ES 10.3 key dates table. The current official Cambridge timetable always takes precedence.

task_categories.C5: Secure Storage, Evidence File & Centre Compliance
task_categories.C6: Coordination with the Principal, Quality Nominee & Departments

priority_levels.compliance: Cambridge-required. Centre status depends on this. Non-negotiable.

recurring_tasks.title: Read Cambridge updates and share what matters
recurring_tasks.description: Read this week's Cambridge International updates — syllabus update notices, Centre bulletins, timetable changes, the list of e-marked subjects. Share anything material with the Principal, the Quality Nominee and the Heads of Department it affects.
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Cambridge updates can change syllabus content, paper structure or which subjects are e-marked. Use the shared exams email address for Cambridge correspondence, not a personal inbox (Exams Officer Handbook §16).

recurring_tasks.title: Check your deadline calendar and the next Cambridge deadline
recurring_tasks.description: Look at your own deadline calendar: what is the next Cambridge deadline, and is your internal deadline for it at least one week earlier? Tell the people who need to act — the Principal (Head of Centre), the Academic Coordinator, Heads of Department, the IT Coordinator or the Facilities Manager. Keep both exam series on one calendar.
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Deadlines are promises to students. Build the calendar backward from each Cambridge deadline and confirm the exact dates with Cambridge every year — they shift slightly from cycle to cycle.

recurring_tasks.title: File this week's exam records in the evidence file
recurring_tasks.description: File the documents created this week — entry records, access-log pages, training registers, access arrangements approvals, incident reports, dispatch receipts, Cambridge correspondence. File them the week they are created, not before an inspection.
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: If it isn't written down, it didn't happen. Cambridge may inspect announced or unannounced — a gap you find in October is a note; the same gap found by an inspector is a finding.

monthly_tasks.title: Monthly secure storage audit
monthly_tasks.description: Audit the secure storage and log the audit: check locks and seals, check that every access in the log has a date, time, person and purpose, and that only the two or three authorised key holders hold keys or codes. Report the findings to the Principal.
monthly_tasks.first_time_guide: The access log is one of the first things a Cambridge inspector asks for. No spare keys in a drawer; anyone else who enters is supervised by a key holder.

termly_tasks.title: Post-series review with the Quality Nominee
termly_tasks.description: Lead a structured review of the last series with the Quality Nominee — September for May/June, March for October/November. Look at the incident log, stakeholder feedback and where procedures did not work. Outputs go to the Principal and the Board: a review report, updated procedures, your professional development plan and budget recommendations.

termly_tasks.title: Keep your Exams Officer training current
termly_tasks.description: Record your training: the Cambridge Exams Officer course within 6 months of appointment, at least two Cambridge refresher webinars a year, and the Eduversal network Exams Officer training held twice a year. Keep certificates and attendance records in your evidence file.
evidence_required: Training records in the evidence file

tasks.title: Start-of-year Centre check
tasks.description: Confirm with the Principal that the school's Cambridge Centre status is active. Check the evidence file holds the appointment letters for you and the Quality Nominee. Confirm the two or three authorised key holders and the handover procedure when one is absent. Complete or update your school's Exam Operations Annex — secure storage, key holders, courier, e-marking equipment, rooms at 1.25 m spacing, internal contacts, Cambridge accounts. If the school separates the Cambridge Coordinator and Exams Officer roles, agree the split in writing.

tasks.title: Build and share this year's deadline calendar
tasks.description: Put the Cambridge dates for both series in one calendar — entries, access arrangements, Key Times, results, post-results services — and set your own internal deadline at least one week before each Cambridge deadline. Take the dates from the current Cambridge timetable and the ES 10.3 key dates table. Share it with the Principal, the Academic Coordinator and the Heads of Department. Check it against the four EASE Weeks: where a Cambridge exam falls in the same week as a Synchronized Test, the exam replaces the Synchronized Test for those grades and subjects — follow the grade tab in the live EASE Schedule 26-27.

tasks.title: May/June results — release, analysis and post-results services
tasks.description: With the Head of Centre, download the Statement of Results from Cambridge International Direct and give each candidate their statement securely — results are confidential and never posted publicly. Lead the results analysis with the Principal: grade distributions against Cambridge benchmarks, component performance, predicted against actual grades, trends. Heads of Department receive subject reports. Manage post-results requests with families by each Cambridge deadline; a review of marking can lower a grade, so the family must accept that risk first. After the awards release, check the Outstanding Cambridge Learner Awards before any announcement.

tasks.title: Confirm the October/November entries
tasks.description: By September, standard October/November entries should already be closed. Check the Entry Confirmation Report from Cambridge against the approved list — every candidate, subject, tier and component — and tell students and parents the confirmed entries and fees. Names must match the passport or national ID character by character.
tasks.first_time_guide: Wrong entries mean students sit wrong papers. Review every entry twice before the Head of Centre approves the submission.

tasks.title: Prepare the October/November series
tasks.description: Confirm the final timetable and resolve any clashes with an approved method. Make sure approved access arrangements are planned for every relevant exam. Select, train and brief invigilators — safeguarding checks done, annual training complete, code of conduct signed — and run a short scenario briefing (fire alarm, sick candidate, phone found) and the malpractice briefing. Prepare rooms: desks 1.25 m apart, seating plan, visible clock, signs. At the same time, start May/June planning for the next cohort.

tasks.title: Receive and store the secure materials
tasks.description: On arrival, check that seals are intact and the contents match the dispatch list, sign and date the receipt, and store everything in secure storage straight away. If a seal is broken, do not open further — contact Cambridge the same day and record everything. Check the Key Times for your location on the Cambridge website.
evidence_required: Receipt logged in the secure storage register

8-15.phase: Late September to mid-November — October/November exams

tasks.title: October/November exam administration
tasks.description: Run each exam day: packets collected from secure storage as close to the start as possible and opened in front of candidates; every candidate in the exam or under Full Centre Supervision at the Key Time; approved access arrangements delivered and logged; be reachable while every exam runs. Count scripts against the attendance register, then despatch them the day of the exam wherever possible and within 2 working days (48 hours for e-marking uploads) — five working days after the exam is Cambridge's own deadline. Report suspected malpractice through the Head of Centre on the same day, or by 12:00 the next working day.

tasks.title: Supply the data for the Annual Examinations Report
tasks.description: Each November the Board receives an Annual Examinations Report: participation, outcomes, compliance status, incidents and budget. You supply the data; the Principal presents it.

tasks.title: Verify and hand over certificates
tasks.description: Cambridge sends certificates about three months after results. Check each certificate against the results data before you hand it over, log every handover with a signature, and send alumni certificates by registered post or on collection with ID.

tasks.title: Record the approved subject list and open the access arrangements list
tasks.description: Subject selection happens the term before entries. Record the combination the Principal or Academic Coordinator approved for each May/June candidate, including tier decisions. Open the access arrangements list for the cohort now, together with subject selection — gathering diagnostic evidence takes months.

tasks.title: October/November results — release and analysis
tasks.description: With the Head of Centre, download the Statement of Results and give each candidate their statement securely. Lead the analysis with the Principal and send subject-level reports to Heads of Department; the Principal shares the whole-school analysis with the Academic Board. Findings feed the school's improvement plan.

tasks.title: Post-results services for the October/November series
tasks.description: Manage clerical re-checks, reviews of marking and return of scripts with families and teachers, by each Cambridge deadline (typically about three weeks after results — confirm with the current Cambridge timetable). Advise honestly: a review of marking makes sense when a result is far below prediction and internal moderation supports a marking-error theory.

22.phase: Late January — annual examinations policy review

tasks.title: Review the examinations policy
tasks.description: After the October/November series, review the school's examinations policy with the Quality Nominee and the Principal, with version control and a change log.
evidence_required: Policy reviewed and change log updated

tasks.title: Submit the May/June entries
tasks.description: Submit the May/June entries in Cambridge International Direct before the deadline (ES 10.3 lists 15 February as the typical date — confirm with the current Cambridge timetable). Review every entry twice, the Head of Centre approves the submission, then check the Entry Confirmation Report against the approved list and tell students and parents the confirmed entries and fees. Lower Secondary Checkpoint uses the May series.

26.phase: Late February / March — access arrangements and the Annual Declaration

tasks.title: Submit the May/June access arrangements applications
tasks.description: Submit each application with its evidence by the Cambridge deadline (ES 10.3 lists 1 March as the typical date). Apply again for every series — Cambridge does not carry an approval over.

tasks.title: Prepare the Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration
tasks.description: Prepare the Annual Declaration for the Principal to sign, typically by March, and file the signed copy in the evidence file.

tasks.title: Prepare the May/June series
tasks.description: Confirm the final timetable and resolve clashes; plan the delivery of every approved access arrangement; train and brief invigilators, including the scenario and malpractice briefings; prepare rooms at 1.25 m spacing; receive and store secure materials as they arrive. Name who covers for you if you are ill — the key holder handover procedure in your Exam Operations Annex.

31-35.phase: Late April to early June — May/June exams

tasks.title: May/June exam administration — peak operations
tasks.description: Same daily discipline as October/November, over the longest series of the year: Key Times, secure storage, invigilation quality, access arrangements delivered and logged, scripts counted and despatched the day of the exam wherever possible and within 2 working days (48 hours for e-marking uploads; five working days is Cambridge's own deadline). Record circumstances for special consideration the same day and submit by the Cambridge deadline. Report suspected malpractice through the Head of Centre on the same day, or by 12:00 the next working day.
tasks.first_time_guide: This is the role's hardest period. Plan leave around it, not into it. Candidate welfare comes first in any incident; security of papers comes straight after safety of people.

tasks.title: Verify and hand over certificates
tasks.description: Cambridge sends certificates about three months after results. Check each certificate against the results data before you hand it over, log every handover with a signature, and send alumni certificates by registered post or on collection with ID.

tasks.title: Record the approved subject list and open the access arrangements list
tasks.description: Subject selection happens the term before entries. Record the combination the Principal or Academic Coordinator approved for each October/November candidate, including tier decisions, and open the access arrangements list for the cohort. By September, standard October/November entries should already be closed.

tasks.title: Year-end records check
tasks.description: Walk the inspection readiness checklist: storage logs complete and signed, training records current, declarations submitted, malpractice files in order. Keep records for the retention periods in the network standards and current Cambridge rules. Unused question papers and leftover scripts are destroyed by cross-shredding only after the post-results window closes, with a destruction log signed off by the Principal.

writes_to: School Exams Officer evidence file (Exams Officer Handbook §14)

provenance.regulatory_sources: Cambridge Handbook for Centres (current edition); Eduversal Academic Standards Sections 3 and 10 (ES 10.3 key dates table); Cambridge Centre Agreement (per school)
provenance.framework_sources: Curriculum Module: Exams Officer Handbook 26-27; Induction Module: Exams Officers 26-27; Quality Ecosystem: School Principals Checklist 26-27 (Cambridge Compliance); Quality Ecosystem: External Exams & Admissions 26-27
provenance.operational_pattern_source: Rewritten 2026-10-01 against the live Academic Services 26-27 documents. Week keys follow the 40-week template in _academic-year-arc.json; the live Cambridge timetable sets the real dates each year.
provenance.known_conflict: Script despatch: the Exams Officer Handbook §11 says 'within 2 working days of the exam (48 hours for e-marking uploads)'; ES 10.3 says the day of the exam wherever possible, with five working days after the exam as the Cambridge deadline and 48 hours as the Eduversal internal target. The tasks state both: the handbook's 2-working-day target and Cambridge's five-working-day deadline. Key holders: the Exams Officer Handbook §6 allows two or three authorised key holders; ES 10.3.1 names only the Principal and the Exams Officer.

naming_clarification: The platform key 'cambridge_coordinator' is the existing ah_sub_role value in the codebase (`ah_sub_roles[]` includes 'cambridge_coordinator'). The live documents call the role 'Exams Officer' (Curriculum Module: Exams Officer Handbook 26-27), carried in many schools by the Cambridge Coordinator. The schema retains the platform key for backward compatibility with weekly_templates / weekly_progress doc-id construction; UI labels can show 'Cambridge Coordinator / Exams Officer'.
